catalog_quote: The primary stress pattern in Migabac is word initial with an alternating secondary stress throughout the phonological word. This represents a typical trochaic pattern. ... The example below illustrates this 312121 pattern. ... However, this pattern is not entirely consistent. Many times primary stress is found on the second syllable with an alternating secondary stress. Some data revealed that the alternating stress is also inconsistent. ... Reduplicated two syllable words typically reflect a 1321 pattern. ... adjectives can be derived by the addition of a –ne suffix. In this specific context, the primary stress is consistently found on the penultimate syllable; that is, the syllable immediately preceding the suffix. ... audit.reasoning: The classification 'variable' (primary stress on one of the first two syllables, default initial with rightward trochaic secondaries, first-vs-second unpredictable and speaker-variable) rests on the only published phonology of Migabac, McEvoy 2005 (SIL Data Papers 47), which we hold; the deciding quotation, the exception quotation and the domain quotation are all verbatim at the cited pages (275-277), and the author explicitly rules out syllable count and syllable weight as conditioners, so the coding faithfully reflects the source. The description is semi-instrumental (Speech Analyzer intensity graphs, two speakers, appendix data), which is as good as SIL sketches get. The only plausibly better source is the same author's 2008 381-page M.A. discourse grammar, which is not openly available (DIU lists it without a PDF, SIL-PNG record empty, Wayback offline/no capture, pnglanguages.sil.org
